correctness.rationale: All q>=7 eligible: two-witness property iff all single deletions satisfy the rank-five random-tournament theory, by explicit five-round EF and extension sentences. Every four-set over a prime field is affine-square equivalent to {0,1,x,y}; two independent exact 16-pattern censuses on all 24 eligible primes through 211 agree. Nonprime q=27 is excluded by a 32-witness pigeonhole count. For all finite fields q>=223 the full indicator expansion, degree-one/two exact correlations and degree-three/four Weil bounds yield N>1. This is a proof of the infinite classification with finite computations confined to a finite rigorously bounded range.

originality.rationale: The principal existing one-witness P4 theorem does not imply two-witness or deletion-stable P4. Orders 67/71/79/83 have P4 but min witness 1, so the strengthened property differs on named mathematical objects. Direct full-text source comparisons did not locate the global two-witness cutoff at 107. Priority remains subject to unlocated stronger results.
residual_risks: The 1971 publisher full PDF was not accessible in this review; the publisher abstract and a cited technical summary were read, so no full-text noncoverage claim is made for that item.
Some unindexed fault-tolerant/two-fold extension article or unpublished table might independently contain the result; searches are not proof of global novelty.

value.rationale: A sharp natural vertex-deletion stability threshold for first-order rank-five approximation to the random tournament is a substantive, non-implied robustness classification. It separates P4 at 67,71,79,83 from two-fold P4 beginning exactly at 107, with a uniform finite-field theorem backed by character sums and a bounded exact census. The exact number 107 is necessary for this deletion tolerance and is not an arbitrary sample statistic.
